identity: Seeing a signal is not enough. We need to know whether the radar could observe what we want to interpret.

mission.title: What QHANTAR is
mission.what: QHANTAR takes one real NISAR GUNW product (a geocoded unwrapped interferogram) and, for every pixel, asks whether this specific interferometric pair allows a hypothetical downhill motion of the slope to be interpreted. It crosses three things: the slope geometry from a DEM, the radar's native line of sight stored in the product, and the coherence and connected components measured for this pair.
not: It does not detect slope movements automatically.
It does not compute a risk index.
It does not say whether a mountain is stable.
It does not measure displacement from S.
It does not turn coherence into displacement.
It does not read raw phase as a confirmed event.
It does not recover the three components of motion from one line of sight.
It does not guarantee that an 'interpretable' area has detectable motion.
mission.slow: A single 12-day pair cannot be presented as a detector of slow landslides: 5 cm/year is about 1.6 mm in 12 days, which can sit below the noise of one interferogram.
mission.prior: Not a new idea: the slope–line-of-sight relation and visibility indices already exist (Notti et al. 2010; van Natijne et al. 2022). QHANTAR applies them after the fact to one concrete NISAR pair, with its native geometry and its measured quality.

mountain.title: Terrain of the scene
mountain.body: Slope and downhill aspect are computed from the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM resampled to the 80 m GUNW grid, using metric coordinates (UTM 19S). Pixels with slope below the minimum have no defined downhill direction.

radar.title: Radar evidence, layer by layer
radar.body: Phase, coherence and connected components are shown separately. They are never combined into a single score.
radar.phase_note: Phase in radians, not displacement. Its large-scale fringes across the whole scene are most likely atmospheric or ionospheric; QHANTAR does not interpret them.
radar.cc_note: Value 0 is treated as invalid by inference: neither the file nor ASF documentation defines it. The file only contains 0 and 1.

obs.title: Slope–LOS observability
obs.body: S is the projection of a hypothetical downhill unit motion on the radar line of sight. |S| close to 1: motion along the line of sight; close to 0: motion almost invisible to this geometry. S is not a measurement of motion.

state_desc.1: valid geometry, |S| and coherence above threshold, valid component
state_desc.0: layover, shadow, no data, invalid component, flat, or low |S| and low coherence

passport.title: Evidence passport
passport.h1_q: Do pixels flagged as layover or shadow show lower coherence and more invalid components than geometrically valid pixels?
passport.confound: Part of the difference is a steep-slope effect: valid pixels on slopes ≥ 30° also show lower coherence. See docs/validation-h1.md.
passport.pending: H2 (contrast with the R index), H3 (native LOS vs heading/incidence approximation) and H4 (known active areas of La Paz) are pending.

footer: QHANTAR · NASA Space Apps 2026 · Dancing with the SARs. Results come from one NISAR PROVISIONAL product; every number on this page is read from results.json.

cover.b3: In the mountains, no motion on the radar does not mean no motion on the ground.

cover.handover_label: From the illustration to the real data
cover.handover_body: From here on, every image is a real layer over La Paz, from the NISAR product or the DEM it is paired with, and every figure comes from results.json.
cover.alt_hillshade: Real shaded relief of La Paz from the Copernicus DEM

relief.title: The terrain
relief.body: The slope from the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, brought to the product's 80 m grid. Flat ground has no downhill direction.

coherence.title: The quality of the pair
coherence.body: How alike the two passes are, 12 days apart. It says whether the signal is reliable. It does not say whether the radar looks along the slope.

sens.title: The radar geometry
sens.body: |S| is how much of a downhill motion would land on the product's native line of sight. It is not a measure of motion.

state.title: The four states
state.figlabel: of the La Paz crop is interpretable
state.body: Geometry and quality are crossed, never merged: every pixel gets a state and the reason for it.

cover.states_lead: Share of pixels in the La Paz crop and in the whole radar footprint.
cover.thresholds: Thresholds: |S| ≥ {s} and coherence ≥ {c}, both configurable. In La Paz, {f} % is flat ground (mostly the El Alto altiplano), not a radar failure.
cover.note_ai_footer: The cover animation is an AI-generated illustration (Higgsfield, Kling 4.0); it is not data.
cover.close_title: One sheet, one observation, every source in view.
